documents: Published paper: Estève et al. (2022), Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL100158 (PDF, 10 pages; supporting information not supplied)

entry.evidence: no regional scale seismic imaging of the BSCM crustal and upper mantle structures is yet available to verify or refute the subduction initiation hypothesis

steps.action: The authors pose the problem: the crustal and upper-mantle structure of the slowly converging Beaufort Sea margin is unimaged, so the subduction-initiation idea can be neither verified nor refuted.
steps.quote: no regional scale seismic imaging of the BSCM crustal and upper mantle structures is yet available to verify or refute the subduction initiation hypothesis

steps.action: The authors take from Hyndman et al. (2005) the interpretation that about 2 mm/yr of convergence may be developing into incipient subduction.
steps.quote: Such convergence may be developing into a rare case of incipient subduction.

steps.action: The authors assemble archival IRIS records from 27 stations for 1,080 regional earthquakes (2012-2021), band-pass filter them (2-15 Hz), hand-pick P and S arrivals and cull by pick count and a 1.7 s residual cut, leaving 13,470 P and 13,329 S times from 925 events.
steps.quote: We visually inspect seismograms and manually pick clear P- and S-wave arrivals.

steps.action: The authors invert the travel times with LOTOS for 3-D VP and VS and for hypocentres, using an iteratively updated 1-D starting model, ray-density node grids at four orientations averaged into one model, LSQR, five iterations and chosen damping and smoothing values.
steps.quote: We use the Local Tomography Software (LOTOS) to estimate the three-dimensional isotropic seismic velocity structure

steps.action: The authors run checkerboard tests with ±7% anomalies at 70 km and 50 km scales, with realistic noise and full relocation; recovery is good under most of the continent at 50 km scale but poor beneath the Beaufort Sea.
steps.quote: Checkerboard test models consist of an alternating pattern of fast and slow velocity anomalies

steps.action: The authors run an odd/even test, inverting the two halves of the event list separately; the main anomalies agree, while the NE Brooks Range high and the offshore features do not.
steps.quote: two independent inversions of data subsets with the odd and even index numbers of the earthquake sequence respectively

steps.action: The authors report the relocated seismicity: hypocentres are mostly shallower than the initial locations, most lie at 0-20 km depth (placing the brittle-ductile transition at 20-30 km), and offshore relocations are uncertain.
steps.quote: implying that the brittle-ductile transition zone occurs between 20 and 30 km depth where seismicity decreases rapidly

steps.action: The authors check the relocated events against mapped geology: Richardson Mountains alignments follow mapped faults, and Canning River epicentres follow the strike-slip segments linked to the 2018 Kaktovik sequence.
steps.quote: This north-south feature correlates well with mapped fault traces

steps.action: The authors identify in the velocity models a very low-velocity anomaly that dips to the northwest beneath the eastern Romanzof Uplift and extends below 40 km depth and below the earlier Moho model; they name it the RUA.
steps.quote: the very low-velocity anomaly (max δV = −15%) in northernmost Yukon below the eastern part of the Romanzof uplift

steps.action: The authors run synthetic structural tests and cite the checkerboard results to show that the long-wavelength RUA can be recovered at this location and is not an artefact of azimuthal ray coverage.
steps.quote: is a robust feature in our velocity models, as highlighted by synthetic structural tests

steps.action: The authors derive VP/VS from the ratio of absolute velocities; it ranges from 1.6 to 1.9, does not follow the velocity anomalies, and is highest along the margin northwest of the RUA.
steps.quote: VP/VS values range between 1.6 and 1.9 and the distribution does not appear to correlate spatially

steps.action: The authors compare absolute VP, VS and VP/VS at 20 km depth with laboratory rock-velocity compilations; the RUA reads as felsic and the crust east and west of it as more mafic.
steps.quote: which indicate felsic compositions such as quartz mica schist, felsic granulite, granite-granodiorite

steps.action: The authors note that regional Moho estimates follow the ~7 km/s VP contour except beneath the Romanzof Uplift, and interpret the RUA as locally thickened crust with a Moho near 50 km.
steps.quote: We therefore interpret the RUA to represent locally thickened crust (∼50 km depth Moho; Figure 4).

steps.action: The authors compare the inferred Moho with an independent receiver-function Moho at station TA.D28M inside the RUA (33.5 ± 1.6 km); the two do not match.
steps.quote: This is shallower than the inferred base of the RUA at ∼50 km depth

steps.action: The authors keep the thickened-crust interpretation and attribute the mismatch to heterogeneity or anisotropy in the receiver-function data, an auxiliary, rather than revising the hypothesis.
steps.quote: [...] evidence of heterogeneity and/or anisotropy in the receiver function data that may further reflect weak deformation fabrics

steps.action: The authors explain the aseismic RUA by the weakness of felsic rock and state two rival scenarios: aseismic creep within a narrow onshore margin, or deformation taken up offshore with strain rates too low onshore.
steps.quote: Alternatively, the lack of seismicity may imply that current deformation occurs offshore further north within the Beaufort fold-and-thrust belt

steps.action: The authors keep the claim of locally thick-skinned crustal thickening beneath the RUA, set it against thin-skinned deformation offshore, and say neither scenario requires or precludes subduction initiation.
steps.quote: locally thickened crust (∼50 km depth Moho) beneath the RUA is likely the result of shortening and stacking of weak igneous and sedimentary rocks

steps.action: The authors leave the subduction-initiation hypothesis open and name the data needed to test it: GPS deployments and offshore seismic stations.
steps.quote: Deployments of GPS stations across the BSCM and offshore seismic station coverage would be needed

tree.answer: Slow convergence at the Beaufort margin, possibly incipient subduction; the structure is unimaged
No; crustal velocity structure is latent and must be inferred from travel times
Image VP, VS and VP/VS of the crust and uppermost mantle and interpret them tectonically
Two deformation scenarios (onshore aseismic creep vs offshore accommodation); subduction initiation stated but not tested
No discriminating predictions are derived; the scenarios are left undistinguished
Conditions found: natural regional earthquakes recorded on archival networks
Partly: RUA survives checkerboard, structural and odd/even tests; offshore unresolved; receiver-function Moho mismatches
Thickened felsic crust kept as interpretation; subduction initiation neither required nor precluded
No review file supplied; acknowledgments thank two reviewers

end.claim: A robust northwest-dipping crustal low-velocity anomaly beneath the Romanzof Uplift (felsic VP/VS 1.70-1.78) is interpreted as locally thickened crust (~50 km Moho) from shortening and stacking of weak rocks; its aseismic deformation is accommodated either onshore or offshore, and neither reading requires or precludes subduction initiation.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the LOTOS travel-time tomography revealing the Romanzof Uplift Anomaly, there would be no thickened-crust claim.

gates.evidence: Action: the data are archival IRIS/TA records picked without hypothesis-specific design; the subduction hypothesis motivates the study only generally (p. 2). Claim: the RUA as a model feature faced synthetic structural and checkerboard tests it could have failed (p. 6), and the thickened-crust reading faced an independent receiver-function Moho that mismatched and was protected (p. 7); the deformation scenarios and the subduction hypothesis faced no test (p. 8). Registration: damping, smoothing and the starting model were tuned on the data (p. 3); nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: LSQR iterative sparse least-squares algorithm (Paige & Saunders 1982)

novelty_claims.quote: We present new seismic velocity models (VP, VS and VP/VS) of the Beaufort Sea continental margin (BSCM)
no regional scale seismic imaging of the BSCM crustal and upper mantle structures is yet available
Here we develop new three-dimensional seismic velocity models (VP, VS and VP/VS) of the crust and uppermost mantle

limits: Only the main paper was supplied. Checks in the supporting information (Figures S1-S24) are coded from the main-text descriptions only. No peer-review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence; the acknowledgments mention two reviewers. Sub-claims and their statuses: (1) the 3-D VP and VS models are estimate_with_resolution, about 50 km lateral resolution beneath most of the continent and unresolved offshore above 50 km depth (p. 4); (2) the brittle-ductile transition at 20-30 km is estimate_with_resolution, but offshore relocations are highly uncertain (p. 4); (3) the felsic RUA composition is best_explanation, by comparison with laboratory compilations (p. 7); (4) the onshore-versus-offshore deformation scenarios reach no_conclusion (p. 8); (5) the subduction-initiation hypothesis is explicitly left untested, no_conclusion (p. 8). The thickened-crust reading rests on a velocity-contour proxy for the Moho and conflicts with a receiver-function Moho of 33.5 km; the authors resolve this only by suggesting receiver-function heterogeneity, and coding that step as P with return_after_failure is the coder's inference. The damping and smoothing choices are justified, but their effect on the RUA is not shown in the main text. The starting 1-D model was iterated on the same data. No alternative interpretation of the low velocities (for example heat flow or fluids) is discussed in the main text; supplement references to heat-flow papers suggest one may be discussed there (inference). The composition is coded none_fits: the walk is estimation followed by interpretation, with no crucial test, no capability-first order and no repeated natural cases fitted to a regularity. Gate coding involves judgement.

disagreements.support: The velocity models and the aseismic thickened crust are explained without invoking subduction initiation, though they do not exclude it.
disagreements.quote: Neither interpretation requires nor precludes a subduction initiation process.
